properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 12 at 3:59PM EDT by NWS Indianapolis IN
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Indianapolis IN has issued a
Flood Warning for the following rivers in Indiana...

Big Blue River at Carthage.

Clifty Creek at Hartsville.

.Copious rainfall in the past 24 hours, totaling as much as 5 inches
in Bartholomew County and 8 inches in Rush County, are quickly
bringing flooding to the Big Blue River and Clifty Creek today.
Rainfall will taper off the rest of the day, with additional amounts
expected to be under four tenths of an inch.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Blue River at Carthage.

* WHEN...From this afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 11.0 feet, Extensive flooding is in progress. Many
local roads flood and are impassable to most vehicles. A few
evacuations are necessary in southern parts of Carthage, extreme
southern sections of Knightstown, eastern Raysville and a few
rural areas of northwest Rush County. Used auto parts yard in
Carthage is flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 2:30 PM EDT Wednesday the stage was 6.9 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.1
feet late tonight.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
To escape rising water, take the shortest path to higher ground.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

The next statement should be issued Thursday morning by around 700
AM EDT.

properties.instruction:
A Heat Advisory means that hot weather conditions are occurring or
expected. This will create a situation in which heat illnesses are
possible.

Never, ever, leave children or pets alone in enclosed vehicles, not
even for a few minutes. Car interiors can reach lethal temperatures
in a matter of minutes.

Stay indoors and seek air-conditioned buildings. Drink water more
than usual, and avoid dehydrating alcoholic, sugary, or caffeinated
drinks. Dress for the heat by wearing lightweight and light colored
clothing. Eat small meals and eat more often. Monitor those with a
higher vulnerability to heat, including small children. Check in on
family, friends, and neighbors, especially the elderly. If engaging
in outdoor activity, take longer and more frequent breaks and avoid
the hottest parts of the day.

The Montana Department of Environmental Quality has issued an air
quality alert for Beaverhead, Deer Lodge, Granite, Silver Bow,
Madison, Missoula, Ravalli counties in effect until 9AM on 08/13/2026
An Air Quality Alert means that particulates have been trending
upwards and that an exceedance of the 24 hour National Ambient Air
Quality Standard (NAAQS) has occurred or may occur in the near
future.

Elevated particulate levels from wildfire smoke

As of 8AM on 08/12/2026, particulate levels in Dillon are Unhealthy.

As of 8AM on 08/12/2026, particulate levels in Frenchtown and
Missoula are Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

As of 8AM on 08/12/2026, particulate levels in Billings, Butte,
Choteau, Columbia Falls, Cut Bank, Great Falls, Hamilton, Havre,
Helena, Lewistown, Libby, Malta, Sleeping Giant, Thompson Falls and
West Yellowstone are Moderate.

When air quality is Unhealthy... State and local health officials
recommend that people with respiratory or heart disease, the elderly,
and children should avoid prolonged exertion; everyone else should
limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups... State and local
health officials recommend that people with respiratory or heart
disease, the elderly and children should limit prolonged exertion.

When air quality is Moderate... State and local health officials
recommend that unusually sensitive people should consider reducing
prolonged or heavy exertion.

For more information visit the Montana Department of Environmental
Quality at http://todaysair.mtdeq.us

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued August 12 at 12:47AM PDT by NWS Pendleton OR
properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air Agency,
and the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency have issued an Air Quality
Alert until further notice.

An Air Quality Alert has been issued for Benton, Columbia, Franklin,
Kittitas, Walla Walla and Yakima counties until further notice due
to expected wildfire smoke from regional fires. Expect some clearing
out and intermittent good air quality but with significant fires on
the landscape conditions can worsen quickly to unhealthy air. Be sure
to check air monitors in your area before outdoor activities.

People can take the following precautions to protect their health:

* Follow local burn restrictions to prevent deteriorating air
quality.
* Avoid strenuous outdoor activity in smoky conditions.
* People with heart or lung problems and young children are
especially vulnerable. These people should stay indoors while
smoke levels are high.
* Use certified High Efficiency Particulate Air (HEPA) filters in
indoor heating ventilation, cooling, and air purification systems.
* Avoid using wood-burning stoves and other sources of indoor smoke
if possible.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
Information from the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.yakimacleanair.org or call 509-834-2050.
Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.

properties.description:
The Washington State Department of Ecology, Benton Clean Air Agency,
and the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency  have issued an Air Quality
Alert until further notice.

For the Smoke Air Quality Alert, wildfires burning in the region
combined with forecasted conditions will cause air quality to reach
unhealthy levels.

Pollutants in smoke can cause burning eyes, runny nose, aggravate
heart and lung diseases, and aggravate other serious health
problems. Limit outdoor activities and keep children indoors if it
is smoky. Please follow medical advice if you have a heart or lung
condition.

Information from the Washington Department of Ecology web site is
available at http://www.ecy.wa.gov/air.html or call 360-407-6000.
Information from the Yakima Regional Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.yakimacleanair.org or call 509-834-2050.
Information from the Benton County Clean Air Agency web site is
available at http://www.bentoncleanair.org or call 509-783-1304.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued August 12 at 3:15AM EDT until August 12 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 108 to 112 expected.

* WHERE...Southern Brevard Barrier Islands County.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors. Young children and
pets should never be left unattended in vehicles under any
circumstances. Take extra precautions if you work or spend time
outside. When possible reschedule strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion
and heat stroke. Wear lightweight and loose fitting clothing when
possible. To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety
and Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks
in shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.description:
The warmest stretch of weather so far this summer is expected from
Wednesday through the weekend. High temperatures warming into the
upper 70s or lower 80s each day with lows dipping into the 50s are
expected. Areas of wildfire smoke across the middle Tanana Valley
are already reducing air quality. Light winds are unlikely to
clear out the smoke.

and limiting exposure to smoke is recommended.

Idaho Department of Environmental Quality in Coeur d'Alene
Environmental Protection Agency

...AIR QUALITY ADVISORY FROM THE IDAHO DEPARTMENT OF ENVIRONMENTAL
QUALITY FOR Boundary, Bonner, Counties...

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory because of degraded air quality due to
wildfire smoke. Air Quality Index is forecast to be Unhealthy.

* WHERE...Boundary, Bonner Counties...

* WHEN...Next update 12 PM August 14th.

* IMPACTS...Some members of the general public may experience health
effects; members of sensitive groups may experience more serious
health effects.

elderly, as well as persons with respiratory problems. Those
individuals who are sensitive to increased particulate matter or
smoke are encouraged to avoid prolonged or strenuous outdoor
activity during this advisory. Open burning is prohibited by air
quality rule. It is also recommended that all other individuals
limit prolonged or strenuous activity outdoors.

Coeur d'Alene Regional Office at (208) 769-1422
